hook.text: Condorcet's Jury Theorem: one decision can look obvious until uncertainty changes the frame.

buildup.text: If each person has a 60 percent chance of being correct, a group of 100 has a 99.9 percent chance of a correct majority.

discovery.text: The theorem shows that group size magnifies individual competence. Slightly above chance becomes near certainty.

twist.text: If each person is below 50 percent accuracy, larger groups get worse. The theorem amplifies incompetence just as well.

climax.text: Condorcet's lesson: groups improve decisions only if members are individually competent.

punchline.text: Slightly right, vastly accurate in groups. But slightly wrong, vastly wrong.

quiz.question: When does Condorcet's jury theorem fail?
options: When the jury is too large
When individual members are less than 50% likely to be correct
